replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Oh fr? How do you feel about people using ai to make video games now? Do you think it’s a good thing or a bad thing?

replies.author: fd40
replies.body:
i could talk forever about this topic. all increments in technology previously have moved civilisation forward. induistrial revolution, calculators, computers. but each one wasnt a smooth transition as it brings about significant redundency in the process.

for me. right now it means i actually have the capability, with AI, to create a game as a solo developer. which until now is VERY rare, especially to reach any success.

long term, i see the big AAA staying where it is. i think the industry split between AAA and indie will widen. people will still be waiting for GTA 7 and it will be the best game around at that point it's released. but i also see far more smaller indie successes.

If you can with no experience build a game in 1 prompt. 18 years industry experience and being a very very capable 3D artist/world buiding who is not remotely short on ideas.  i see now specifically as an oppertunity for people like me to leverage our experience and create the games we drempt of creating. But i just hope people use it to realise better their own ideas. not to pump out slop for £. But to shorten the gap between point of inspiration, and point of project completion. and if that can be done without having to deal with huge teams, unpaid overtime, lack of royalties, constant risk of redundancy, then good. but i do also see the day when you could just say "make a game that is as good as" and get a result. that is my personal "event horizon" or "career horizon". one option is joining rather than resisting. being an AI games specialist

replies.author: Plenty-Fox-9219
replies.body:
This "survival" game has two inputs, involves only moving in one direction, has countless set pieces that do nothing, and has no risk of failure.

replies.author: liright
replies.body:
Bro take a look at the falling buildings, the road, the bridge breaking, the cinematic camera when it happens and the seamless transition into a cutscene at the end, those are all things that only AAA games started utilizing in early 2000s. 

It has two inputs but it's one prompt away from having normal controls including braking and acceleration, it's pretty trivial once you have a full 3D world built anyway, I'm guessing the guy wanted it to be subway surfers style so that's why it's that way. 

1.5 years back it was a massive achievement to have AI make a shitty 2D platformer that barely worked. Now we have 3D games with cutscenes and destructible environment. The progress is crazy, even if this still isn't a game I would want to play.
